title: finding(core): `normalize-list-view` still classes the list-view kind `page`, which objectstack main RETIRED from the spec — and the row cannot be deleted today because the PINNED published spec still carries it
body:
`packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts` still classes the list-view kind **`page`**, which objectstack `main` has **retired from the spec**. The two records that partition the derived union no longer compile against it — and ⛔ the row cannot simply be deleted today, because the **pinned published** spec still carries `page`.

Surfaced by the objectui#9860 shape gate on its own first CI run (PR objectui#9877, check `Spec Main Shape Gate`, run `35346702279`, job `105604861812`), and re-measured at source by the filing seat.

## The diagnostic, from the gate's own job log

Against `objectstack-ai/objectstack@784366372ec5` (2026-09-18T12:00:56Z):

```
packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts(205,3): error TS2353 —
Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'page' does not exist in
type 'Record<"list" | "detail", string | null>'.
```

⭐ **Controlled by the gate itself, both legs, same mechanism and same command:** the published `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` leg compiles **exit 0 / 0 diagnostics**; the `main`-built leg is **exit 2 / this one diagnostic**. ⇒ the break is **main-vs-published**, ⛔ not the injection mechanism.

## The mechanism, read at source on objectui `origin/main` `489dd12e` at 2026-09-18T12:59Z

```ts
:156  export type ListViewVisualization = Exclude<ViewType, 'list' | 'detail' | 'page'>;
…
:202  const UNDRAWABLE_VIEW_KINDS: Record<Exclude<ViewType, ListViewVisualization>, string | null> = {
:203    list: null,
:204    detail: null,
:205    page: 'it mounts a published page (bound through `pageName`) in place of rows, …',
:206  };
```

⇒ **two hard-coded `'page'` literals**, at `:156` and `:205`. `ViewType` comes from `@object-ui/types`, itself derived from the spec (objectui#8127). The file's own docblock states the design:

> Total over `Exclude<ViewType, ListViewVisualization>` so the two records together partition the derived union: **a member the spec adds must be classed as drawable or explained HERE, and until it is, neither record compiles.**

⭐ **The guard is working — in the direction it was ⛔ not written for.** It anticipates the spec **adding** a member. What happened is a **removal**: `page` left the union, so `Exclude<…, 'page'>` became a no-op and the record's `page:` key became unknown.

## ⚠️ What makes this NOT a one-line delete

On objectstack `main`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:9285`–`:9364` is a **retirement entry**, ⛔ not drift:

> The `type: 'page'` list-view mount leaves the spec (protocol 18, #17063 …)
> surface: `view.list / view.listViews.* — the list-view type 'page' and its pageName binding`
> `list-view type 'page' and its 'pageName' binding removed (#17063 …)`
> `zero authored 'type: \'page\'' list views in this tree or any consuming app …`

⇒ the removal is **deliberate, registered upstream work**. But objectui is pinned to **published 17.4.0**, where `page` is still in `ViewType` — so deleting the two literals **today** makes `UNDRAWABLE_VIEW_KINDS` non-total against the pin and fails the build the other way.

⚠️ **⛔ The filing seat does ⛔ NOT rule the direction.** Three readings are live and this card's first deliverable is to settle which:
- **A** — objectui drops the two `'page'` literals, riding the `@objectstack/spec` **pin bump** (⛔ not as a rider — the pin bump is its own scripted action).
- **B** — the two literals are written so they are correct under **both** unions, if such a spelling exists.
- **C** — the retirement is contested upstream and `page` returns. ⚠️ The dev that surfaced this recommended a variant of C; the filing seat's reading of registry.ts:9285 is that C would **reverse a landed upstream retirement**, which ⛔ is not this lane's to propose. Recorded as a disagreement, ⛔ not as a ruling.

## Why it matters now

objectui#9860 delivers a CI gate that compiles this repo against spec `main`. ⚠️ **That gate is RED on arrival because of this one diagnostic**, so landing it would put a permanently red advisory check on every objectui PR — the 「advisory 门禁红着进 main 是共享损伤」 shape. ⇒ **this card is the blocker for objectui#9860's landing**, and PR objectui#9877 is deliberately being held, ⛔ not merged.

- `ViewType page retired TS2353`
